title: Pale, then red
setting: A Sunday evening. Okaasan leaves a voicemail for Yuki, who lives on her own, about Yuki's little brother Kenji and his football match that day.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.ja: もしもし、ユキ？お母さんだけど。
lines.kana: もしもし、ゆき？おかあさんだけど。

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji ga ne, kyou sakkaa no shiai de kega shita no. a, daijoubu da kara, shinpai shinaide ne.
lines.ja: ケンジがね、今日サッカーの試合で怪我したの。あ、大丈夫だから、心配しないでね。
lines.kana: けんじがね、きょうさっかーのしあいでけがしたの。あ、だいじょうぶだから、しんぱいしないでね。
lines.english: Kenji got hurt in his football match today. Oh, he's fine, so don't worry.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kaette kita toki, hiza kara chi ga detete, ase mo sugoku kaitete ne.
lines.ja: 帰ってきたとき、膝から血が出てて、汗もすごくかいててね。
lines.kana: かえってきたとき、ひざからちがでてて、あせもすごくかいててね。
lines.english: When he got home, his knee was bleeding, and he was really sweaty too.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kaoiro mo warukatta shi, okaasan, honto ni bikkuri shita wa.
lines.ja: 顔色も悪かったし、お母さん、ほんとにびっくりしたわ。
lines.kana: かおいろもわるかったし、おかあさん、ほんとにびっくりしたわ。
lines.english: And he looked pale, so I got quite a fright.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: hidoi kega shita n ja nai no? tte kiitara, chotto chi ga deta dake da yo tte.
lines.ja: 「ひどい怪我したんじゃないの？」って聞いたら、「ちょっと血が出ただけだよ」って。
lines.kana: 「ひどいけがしたんじゃないの？」ってきいたら、「ちょっとちがでただけだよ」って。
lines.english: I asked him, "You haven't hurt yourself badly, have you?" and he said, "It just bled a bit, that's all."

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sou ieba, kenji tte mukashi kara, chi ga deru to sugu kaoiro ga waruku naru no yo ne.
lines.ja: そういえば、ケンジって昔から、血が出るとすぐ顔色が悪くなるのよね。
lines.kana: そういえば、けんじってむかしから、ちがでるとすぐかおいろがわるくなるのよね。
lines.english: Come to think of it, Kenji's always been like that. The moment he bleeds, he goes pale.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: de, yoru ni natte, shiai o mi ni kiteta onna no ko ga, kenji no wasuremono o motte kite kureta no.
lines.ja: で、夜になって、試合を見に来てた女の子が、ケンジの忘れ物を持ってきてくれたの。
lines.kana: で、よるになって、しあいをみにきてたおんなのこが、けんじのわすれものをもってきてくれたの。
lines.english: Then in the evening, a girl who'd come to watch the match brought round something Kenji had left behind.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: soshitara kenji, kyuu ni kao ga akaku natchatte.
lines.ja: そしたらケンジ、急に顔が赤くなっちゃって。
lines.kana: そしたらけんじ、きゅうにかおがあかくなっちゃって。
lines.english: And Kenji's face suddenly went red.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: hiru wa kaoiro ga warukatta noni, kondo wa kao ga akai no yo.
lines.ja: 昼は顔色が悪かったのに、今度は顔が赤いのよ。
lines.kana: ひるはかおいろがわるかったのに、こんどはかおがあかいのよ。
lines.english: At midday he'd been pale, and now his face was red!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: ato de, kao akai yo, netsu aru no? tte kiitara, atsui dake da yo tte. mata ase kaiteta wa.
lines.ja: あとで、「顔赤いよ、熱あるの？」って聞いたら、「暑いだけだよ」って。また汗かいてたわ。
lines.kana: あとで、「かおあかいよ、ねつあるの？」ってきいたら、「あついだけだよ」って。またあせかいてたわ。
lines.english: Later I said, "Your face is red. Have you got a fever?" and he said, "I'm just hot." He was all sweaty again.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kega shita no mo, ano ko no mae de kakko tsuketa kara kamo ne.
lines.ja: 怪我したのも、あの子の前でかっこつけたからかもね。
lines.kana: けがしたのも、あのこのまえでかっこつけたからかもね。
lines.english: Maybe he even got hurt showing off in front of her.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji ni wa, okaasan kara kiita tte iwanaide ne. jaa ne.
lines.ja: ケンジには、お母さんから聞いたって言わないでね。じゃあね。
lines.kana: けんじには、おかあさんからきいたっていわないでね。じゃあね。
lines.english: Don't tell Kenji you heard it from me, OK? Bye.

choices.english: Kenji hurt his knee at football and came down with a fever that evening, so he's resting.
Kenji fainted at the sight of blood during his match, and a girl had to bring him home.
Kenji got a small cut at football, and Okaasan thinks his red face that evening was about a girl, not a fever.

questions.explanation: Line 2: Kenji got hurt at his football match (kega shita), but Okaasan says he's fine. Line 5: he says it only bled a little. Lines 7-9: when a girl who'd watched the match brought round something he'd left behind, his face suddenly went red. Line 10: he says he's just hot, and in line 11 Okaasan guesses he got hurt showing off in front of her. A is wrong: Okaasan asks about a fever (line 10, netsu aru no?), but Kenji says he's just hot, and nobody says he's resting. B is wrong: Kenji went pale at the blood (lines 4 and 6), but he came home himself (line 3, kaette kita), and the girl only brought round something he'd left behind (line 7).

questions.english: You're home for the weekend with a plaster on your knee. Okaasan spots it and asks, "are, sono hiza dou shita no?" Tell her you hurt it, using kega.
questions.ja: あれ、その膝どうしたの？
questions.kana: あれ、そのひざどうしたの？
questions.romaji: are, sono hiza dou shita no?
questions.answer: Say you hurt it with kega o suru, usually as kega shita, or kega shichatta (I went and got hurt). It's natural to say how it happened: jitensha de kega shita.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, kore? kinou jitensha de kega shichatta.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、これ？昨日自転車で怪我しちゃった。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, this? I hurt it on my bike yesterday.

modelAnswers.romaji: chotto kega shita dake. mou daijoubu da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと怪我しただけ。もう大丈夫だよ。
modelAnswers.english: I just hurt it a bit. It's fine now.

questions.explanation: Okaasan says Kenji kega shita at his match (line 2), asks him hidoi kega shita n ja nai no? (line 5), and guesses why he got hurt: kega shita no mo... (line 11). In Japanese an injury is something you 'do': kega o suru, even by accident, mostly heard as kega shita or kega shichatta. Itaku natta only says it started to hurt, and kizutsuita is mostly for hurt feelings. To name the place, say hiza o kega shita or hiza ni kega o shita, never two o's (not hiza o kega o shita). With your mum, casual is right.

questions.english: Okaasan asked Kenji if he'd hurt himself badly. What did he say?
questions.ja: ケンジは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんじはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: It just bled a bit, that's all.
choices.romaji: chotto chi ga deta dake da yo

choices.english: There was just a bit of haemorrhaging, that's all.
choices.romaji: chotto shukketsu shita dake da yo

choices.english: I just let a bit of blood out, that's all.
choices.romaji: chotto chi o dashita dake da yo

questions.explanation: Line 5: 'chotto chi ga deta dake da yo'. Japanese has no single verb for 'bleed': blood comes out, chi ga deru, the way a fever or a cough does (netsu ga deru, seki ga deru). Okaasan uses the same pair in line 3 (hiza kara chi ga detete) and line 6 (chi ga deru to). B is wrong: shukketsu suru is the medical word for bleeding. A doctor or the news would say it, but not a teenager telling his mum it's nothing. C is wrong: dasu means putting something out yourself, so chi o dashita sounds as if he made it bleed on purpose. Blood from a cut just comes out (deru).

questions.english: You've just walked in after an errand on a hot afternoon. Okaasan asks, "soto, atsukatta?" Answer using ase o kaku, and say you want a shower.
questions.answer: Say you got all sweaty with ase o kaku, usually in the past: ase kaita or ase kaichatta. Then add that you want a shower (shawaa abitai).

modelAnswers.romaji: un, metcha ase kaichatta. shawaa abitai.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、めっちゃ汗かいちゃった。シャワー浴びたい。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I got so sweaty. I want a shower.

modelAnswers.romaji: atsukatta! ase kaita kara, saki ni shawaa abiru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 暑かった！汗かいたから、先にシャワー浴びるね。
modelAnswers.english: It was hot! I'm all sweaty, so I'll have a shower first.

questions.explanation: Okaasan uses it twice. Kenji came home from the match all sweaty (line 3, ase mo sugoku kaitete), and he was sweating again when she asked about his red face (line 10, mata ase kaiteta). 'Sweat' is a verb in English, but Japanese uses the noun ase with kaku, so don't say ase suru. This kaku isn't kaku 'write'. It's the same kaku as in haji o kaku (embarrass yourself). Ase ga deru (sweat comes out) also works, but ase kaita is what people usually say. With your mum, casual is right.

questions.english: Okaasan sits down at the kitchen table and says, "nanka kesa kara, chotto kibun ga warui no yo ne." She has gone pale. Tell her she looks pale, and ask if she's OK.
questions.ja: なんか今朝から、ちょっと気分が悪いのよね。
questions.kana: なんかけさから、ちょっときぶんがわるいのよね。
questions.romaji: nanka kesa kara, chotto kibun ga warui no yo ne.
questions.answer: Tell her she looks pale with kaoiro ga warui (casually kaoiro warui yo), then ask daijoubu?

modelAnswers.romaji: honto da, kaoiro warui yo. daijoubu?
modelAnswers.ja: ほんとだ、顔色悪いよ。大丈夫？
modelAnswers.english: You're right, you look pale. Are you OK?

modelAnswers.romaji: kaoiro ga warui ne. chotto yoko ni nattara?
modelAnswers.ja: 顔色が悪いね。ちょっと横になったら？
modelAnswers.english: You do look pale. Why don't you lie down for a bit?

questions.explanation: Okaasan says it about Kenji three times: kaoiro mo warukatta (line 4), sugu kaoiro ga waruku naru (line 6) and hiru wa kaoiro ga warukatta (line 9). Kaoiro is the colour of your face, and warui says it's a bad colour: pale, unwell. Kao ga shiroi would sound as if she has fair skin, and kao ga aoi is stronger (looking really ill or scared). Her kibun ga warui is how she feels inside. Kaoiro ga warui is what you can see. In casual talk ga often drops (kaoiro warui yo), and daijoubu? usually follows.

questions.english: Okaasan compares how Kenji looked at midday with how he looked in the evening, when the girl came round. What changed?
questions.ja: ケンジの顔は、どう変わりましたか？
questions.kana: けんじのかおは、どうかわりましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji no kao wa, dou kawarimashita ka?

choices.english: At midday he was red from the heat, and in the evening he went pale.
At midday he looked pale, and in the evening his face went red.
He looked pale all day, and in the evening he came down with a fever.

questions.explanation: Line 9: 'hiru wa kaoiro ga warukatta noni, kondo wa kao ga akai no yo'. Kaoiro ga warui means pale (from the blood, lines 4 and 6). Kao ga akai is a red face, which came on suddenly when the girl turned up (line 8, kyuu ni kao ga akaku natchatte). A swaps the two. C is wrong: Okaasan does ask kao akai yo, netsu aru no? (line 10), but Kenji says he's just hot, and she thinks it was about the girl (line 11).
